section: Right to Information Act 2005 - structure, exemptions, amendments and issues
subsections: Political parties under RTI - CIC order and compliance

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT among the six national political parties declared public authorities by the Central Information Commission in June 2013?
accepted.x: The six parties were INC, BJP, CPI, CPI(M), NCP and BSP. The Aam Aadmi Party was not included in that CIC order.
accepted.tq: Find the odd name by recalling the complete six-party list.
accepted.sec: Political parties under RTI - CIC order and compliance

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the demand to bring political parties under the Right to Information Act:
1. It is intended to help check corruption and crony capitalism.
2. It seeks greater scrutiny of illegal foreign contributions.
3. It is linked with the state privileges enjoyed by political parties, including free airtime on Doordarshan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements describe the reasons advanced by activists for bringing political parties under RTI.
accepted.tq: Test the cumulative rationale by checking each policy objective separately.
accepted.sec: Political parties under RTI - CIC order and compliance

accepted.s:
With reference to political parties and the Right to Information Act, consider the following statements:
1. The RTI Act expressly named political parties as public authorities when it was enacted in 2005.
2. The six parties declared public authorities by the CIC did not comply with the order.
3. The issue was pending before the Supreme Court in the position described.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statement 1 is false because the 2005 Act did not expressly name political parties. Statements 2 and 3 are correct in the stated position.
accepted.tq: Spot the wrong historical premise concerning the original wording of the Act.
accepted.sec: Political parties under RTI - CIC order and compliance

accepted.s: The 2026 demand concerning recognised national political parties under the Right to Information framework primarily seeks which of the following?
o: A transparent and auditable electoral-funding system
Abolition of all public funding of elections
Transfer of election expenditure to the Supreme Court
Removal of political parties from Section 2(h)
accepted.x: The 2026 demand was to bring recognised national parties under RTI along with a transparent and auditable electoral-funding system.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise institutional reform rather than an extreme alternative.
accepted.sec: Political parties under RTI - CIC order and compliance

accepted.s: Section 4 of the Right to Information Act, 2005 is primarily associated with which of the following?
o: Imposition of penalty on every delayed applicant
Compulsory adjudication of all RTI appeals by courts
Exemption of personal information from disclosure
Suo motu disclosure by public authorities
accepted.x: Section 4 mandates proactive or suo motu disclosure by public authorities, reducing the need for citizens to file separate applications.
accepted.tq: Match the statutory section with its distinctive function.

accepted.s:
The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended, in the context of RTI, that:
1. Maximum information should automatically be placed in the public domain.
2. Section 8 exemptions should be interpreted narrowly.
3. Citizens should be required to file applications even for routinely publishable information.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 reflect the recommendation. Statement 3 is contrary to proactive disclosure because routinely publishable information should be available without an application.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the purpose of proactive disclosure.

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Information Commission inspected how many offices in how many districts while examining compliance with Section 4(1)(b)?
accepted.x: The inspection covered 258 offices across 18 districts and found violations of Section 4(1)(b).
accepted.tq: Separate the two linked figures and reject reversed or altered numerical pairs.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Action Taken Reports published by the Andhra Pradesh Secretariat from 22 June 2026?
o: They concerned only District Mineral Foundation expenditure.
They concerned six constitutional amendments and were issued by the CIC.
They concerned seven sector white papers and reflected proactive disclosure under Section 4.
They concerned RTI penalties imposed on political parties.
accepted.x: From 22 June 2026, the AP Secretariat published Action Taken Reports on seven sector white papers as an example of disclosure in the spirit of Section 4.
accepted.tq: Use the who-what-when combination to distinguish a current-affairs fact from nearby RTI issues.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: MPLADS works — tracked through the eSAKSHI portal
District Mineral Foundations — exempt from online publication of plans
Section 4(1)(b) — prohibition on suo motu disclosure
Seven sector white papers — disclosure beginning in 2013 through the central RTI portal
accepted.x: MPLADS works are subject to RTI and are tracked through the eSAKSHI portal. The other pairs incorrectly describe the relevant disclosure requirements or dates.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure scheme-portal pair and eliminate mismatched statutory functions and dates.

accepted.s: The RTI Online portal of the Department of Personnel and Training was launched in which year?
accepted.x: The central RTI Online portal, rtionline.gov.in, was launched in 2013 by the Department of Personnel and Training.
accepted.tq: Test the launch year directly against nearby RTI milestone years.
accepted.sec: Online RTI portals - central and Andhra Pradesh

accepted.s: The central RTI Online portal primarily facilitates which of the following?
o: Applications exclusively concerning Andhra Pradesh public authorities
Applications and first appeals concerning central public authorities, with online fee payment
Only appeals against orders of State Information Commissions
Filing of criminal complaints against public servants
accepted.x: The portal at rtionline.gov.in enables filing of RTI applications and first appeals to central public authorities and provides online fee payment.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct jurisdiction and function of the digital platform.
accepted.sec: Online RTI portals - central and Andhra Pradesh

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements best expresses the e-governance approach associated with RTI?
o: Digital disclosure should be mandated so that information is easy to reach.
Only information specifically requested by a citizen should be placed online.
Digital systems should replace every statutory appeal under the RTI Act.
Online disclosure should be restricted to Union public authorities.
accepted.x: The e-governance approach supports mandatory digital disclosure to make information easily accessible to citizens.
accepted.tq: Choose the enabling governance principle rather than an overbroad replacement of statutory mechanisms.
accepted.sec: Online RTI portals - central and Andhra Pradesh

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding recent RTI-related developments:
1. The Supreme Court agreed to examine the conflict between the Digital Personal Data Protection framework and the RTI Act.
2. The Economic Survey 2025–26 called for a re-examination of the RTI Act.
3. A possible ministerial veto over draft policy discussions and service records was among the proposals discussed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements reflect the current debates concerning the interaction of data-protection law, RTI and possible changes to disclosure of policy and service-related records.
accepted.tq: Combine the judicial and policy developments only after verifying that each belongs to the same issue cluster.

accepted.s: The Central Information Commission held that the Board of Control for Cricket in India was not a public authority under Section 2(h)(d) because it was:
o: A body functioning only outside India
Not substantially financed by the government
A constitutional body outside the RTI Act
accepted.x: The CIC held that the BCCI did not qualify under Section 2(h)(d) because it was not substantially financed by the government.
accepted.tq: Apply the statutory qualification test instead of confusing public importance with substantial government financing.

accepted.s: The Central Information Commission directed the CBSE to disclose which of the following after it had denied the information under Section 8(1)(e)?
accepted.x: The CIC ordered the CBSE to disclose answer-book procurement data after the CBSE had invoked the exemption under Section 8(1)(e).
accepted.tq: Distinguish the subject of the disclosure from other current RTI controversies.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Sweden enacts the first RTI law
B. Tamil Nadu becomes the first Indian State to enact an RTI law
C. The RTI Online portal is launched
D. The CIC declares six national political parties public authorities
accepted.x: The sequence is Sweden in 1766, Tamil Nadu in 1997, the central RTI Online portal in 2013 and the CIC order in June 2013; in the ordering used here, the portal launch preceded the June 2013 order.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest and latest milestones, then compare the 2013 events.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the firsts associated with the Right to Information movement?
o: Sweden — first RTI law; Tamil Nadu — first Indian State RTI law; Wajahat Habibullah — first CIC
United Kingdom — first RTI law; Kerala — first Indian State RTI law; Wajahat Habibullah — first CIC
Sweden — first RTI law; Tamil Nadu — first Indian State RTI law; M. Veerappa Moily — first CIC
United States — first RTI law; Tamil Nadu — first Indian State RTI law; Wajahat Habibullah — first CIC
accepted.x: Sweden enacted the first RTI law in 1766, Tamil Nadu enacted the first Indian State RTI law in 1997, and Wajahat Habibullah was the first CIC.
accepted.tq: Use the three independent firsts to eliminate options with one substituted country, State or office-holder.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a criticism or institutional concern relating to the functioning of the RTI regime?
o: Excessive speed in disposal of all RTI applications
accepted.x: The identified concerns include appeal backlogs, vacancies, misuse of Section 8 and threats to activists. Excessive speed in disposal is not listed as a criticism.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the documented governance problem.

accepted.s: The Satark Nagrik Sangathan report of 2025 highlighted gaps in the RTI system particularly in the context of:
o: The launch of the central RTI portal in 2013
The first RTI law of Sweden in 1766
accepted.x: The 2025 report of Satark Nagrik Sangathan flagged gaps as the RTI Act completed 20 years.
accepted.tq: Link the report with its specific anniversary context rather than a general RTI milestone.

accepted.s: Which of the following issues was associated with the weakening of the autonomy of Information Commissions after 2019?
o: Transfer of all RTI matters to local bodies
Concerns regarding institutional independence and functioning of the Commissions
Removal of the right to file first appeals
accepted.x: The post-2019 debate includes concerns that changes weakened the autonomy and institutional independence of Information Commissions.
accepted.tq: Select the institutional consequence rather than an invented repeal or transfer of statutory powers.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Andhra Pradesh Information Commission’s inspection found violations of Section 4(1)(b).
2. The Andhra Pradesh Secretariat’s Action Taken Reports related to seven sector white papers.
3. Both developments concerned proactive disclosure or its spirit rather than the creation of a new exemption under Section 8.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The inspections identified Section 4(1)(b) violations, while the reports on seven white papers represented proactive disclosure. Neither development created a new Section 8 exemption.
accepted.tq: Test whether separate State developments share the same statutory theme without confusing disclosure with exemption.
